scene: A small Roman harbour at warm dawn: a stone gate opens onto a quay where two porters in plain tunics carry clay amphorae up a gangplank onto a moored merchant ship, with coiled rope and a bollard, the whole model sitting on a cut stone-and-water plinth.

An ancient hilltop watchtower of pale stone, its face pierced by a great eye-shaped lens, one cloaked observer on the balcony looking outward over cypress and dust, like a miniature observatory for the act of looking.
A Roman forum in honey-coloured plaster light: an orator in a white toga speaks from a low rostrum, a few listeners on stone steps, and a bronze edict tablet leans against the platform.
A Roman writing corner: a scribe seated at a worn stone desk, reed pen over a wax tablet, a sheet of papyrus and a clay inkpot beside a half-unrolled scroll, north light falling softly.
A Roman road with a milestone: a guide in a russet cloak leads two travellers, while a single aqueduct arch in the middle distance leads a thin thread of water across the view.
A city gate at morning: a messenger in a short tunic has just been sent out, sealed wax tablet in hand, the sender still on the threshold, a little dust lifting from the road.
A palaestra of warm stone and raked sand: an athlete is caught mid-throw with a discus hanging in the air, a low starting line, and two tiny spectators on a step.
Masons raising a small limestone arch: timber centering underneath, one worker setting the keystone, a plumb line, dressed blocks stacked in courses that echo the cut edge of the plinth.
A construction ramp: an ox and two workers draw a dressed stone block on wooden rollers with thick ropes, grooves in the dust, late ochre light.
A mill beside a stone channel: a wooden water-wheel caught mid-turn, paddles dark with water, a miller watching, the race curving around the plinth.

A quiet Roman fragment: a stretch of wall split by one clean vertical crack through stone and plaster, and beside it a moneylender’s bench toppled and broken — the old image of banca rotta — with a few coins, no violence.
Two Romans clasp right hands before a small household altar, the old gesture of fides, a lit clay lamp and a promise-tablet on the table, intimate and still.
A small odeon: curved stone seats, one speaker standing, listeners leaning in, and at the side a clerk hearing accounts read aloud from a wax tablet.
A Roman room opened by a tall window onto a distant aqueduct and hills, a figure just inside looking out, a linen curtain half drawn, daylight itself the subject.
A market under a linen awning: a bronze balance hangs from a chain, one pan slightly lower, a plumb bob beside it, and a few clay jars of grain — hanging and weighing in one still life.
Across a stone counter, one person sets a small sealed bundle into another’s open hands, a third object left apart on the ledge, the quiet act of receiving and setting aside.
A potter’s yard: hands shaping a vessel on a low wheel, bowls of one family drying on a board, a wooden mold leaning on the wall, slip in a shallow bowl.
A quiet atrium: a person rests fingertips on sunlit warm stone while a second figure stands beside them in calm agreement, a shallow pool reflecting the columns.
A herald on the steps of a basilica, one hand cupped to call, a few townspeople turning toward the voice, a posted tablet on the travertine wall, morning light.
A workshop bench: two hands shaping a wooden piece with a plane and an awl, linen apron, curled shavings, no machines — manufacture as making by hand.
A Roman street of basalt pavers: sandaled feet mid-step, a milestone incised with distances, and the empty pedestal of a statue so the foot and the base are the subject.
The porch of a small temple at dawn: a figure’s breath just visible in cool air, a flame bending, a thin thread of incense — spirit as breath, not a ghost.
A plaster study where one clay oil lamp throws a warm pool of light across an open codex, the rest falling into soft shadow, and a tiny morning star in the window.

An intimate Roman room: a person lays a flat hand over the heart while a scribe notes the words — to record is to bring something back to the heart — with a single coral thread on the table as the only red.
A two-wheeled Roman cart just leaving a courtyard, one wheel turned, a mule’s head and shoulder, a draped bundle, dust and a half-open gate suggesting motion without blur.
Two shallow streams meet over pale pebbles and slip past a stone basin, a clay jug tipped so water flows in — a confluence, and influence as an inflow.
A doorway at dusk: a plainly cloaked benefactor sets a bowl of bread into a neighbour’s hands, a small lamp lit, no grandeur, the wish of good made domestic.
The same kind of modest doorway, restrained and not cruel: a cracked bowl, a withered sprig set apart from sound fruit, a shutter askew — spoiling and damage, in the same clay palette as a gift.
A Greek mason kneeling to incise letters into a pale stele, chalk guidelines still visible, chisel and mallet at rest, stone chips scattered, Mediterranean noon softened by dust.
The lower seats of a Greek theatre: a lyre on the stone, a singer standing in the orchestra circle, and two masks hung on the wall, one calm and one harsh.
Two figures in himation seated under a stoa, turned toward each other in dialogue, a scroll half-open on the bench between them, columns receding in warm shade.
A museum-like cut of living soil: roots, a seedling, a beetle, and one butterfly, with a small Greek cup of water beside the plant, life shown as a specimen rather than a garden fantasy.
A Greek hillside opened by the plinth: ochre, clay, and grey strata like a geological specimen, a small figure with a hammer, and a split geode showing dull crystals.
A Greek fountain house: a bronze lion-head spout, a woman filling a three-handled hydria, wet stone darkened by water, a shallow channel crossing the plinth.
A dim Greek room with a small aperture: a shaft of sunlight lays the bright silhouette of a sprig on the plaster wall, light writing an image, a bronze mirror catching a second glint.
A courtyard sundial on a stone block, the gnomon’s shadow exact across incised hour lines, a figure paused to read it, a wax chronicle tablet on a nearby bench.
Psyche without kitsch: a young woman in a pale chiton seated on stone, a single butterfly just lifting from her open palm, a clay lamp beside her, the Greek image of the soul.
Two draped Greek figures on a bench, one leaning in to listen, a hand light on the other’s forearm, a tragic mask set aside unworn — sympathy as feeling-with, suffering kept quiet.
A night study in Athens: a philosopher bent over a scroll by one oil lamp, a second cup waiting, an olive sprig in a small vessel, love of wisdom in an almost empty plaster room.
Metamorphosis on a stone ledge: a split chrysalis, a moth with muted clay-and-cream wings drying, the old skin beside it, a sprig of fennel, change of form with no glow.

A Hellenistic rooftop at late dusk, still lit like a warm museum model: an astronomer with a simple sighting staff, three pale stars, a small star-mark freshly painted on a tablet, and one cracked roof tile for the ill-starred.
Two Greek figures measuring a column drum with a rod and a knotted cord, bronze calipers on the ground, the stone pavement faintly gridded, linen and warm limestone.
A mosaicist kneeling on a half-finished floor, setting tesserae one by one into wet mortar to compose a dolphin; trays of coloured stones beside him
A porter bears a heavy basket of purple-green figs on the shoulder and head.
A Roman storeroom: tall dolia jars hold grain, bound by iron hoops; a keeper holds a ring of keys while a tenant farmer holds out a sack
A Roman bronze-smith's officina: an anvil, a glowing hearth, a smith hammering a blade, finished tools hanging on the wall as proof of making
A crossroads inn at dusk: travellers arrive from three roads at once, lanterns being lit, a host stepping out to greet them
A Roman sentry stands at a fixed post beside a statue on its pedestal at a city corner; a bookseller's fixed stall opposite
A small procession passes through a narrow arch: leaders go ahead, an elder steps aside to yield, footprints showing those who went before
A hand presses a stamp down into a large mound of wax, the wax bulging under the pressure.
A magenta racing court fills the plinth: a chariot rounds the curve, a magenta pennant flying, the track itself the colour.
A broad flight of temple steps; a child climbing them one by one, each step a different shade of stone from light to dark, an elder already at the top
A shepherd driving a flock along a hillside path with a crook while a small open-air stage nearby shows an actor mid-gesture — driving and acting
A Roman atrium with ancestor masks and a painted family tree on the wall; a newborn in a cradle beneath it, generations looking down
An olive harvest under a tree: one figure gathers fallen olives into a basket, another sorts them on a cloth, a third reads a scroll in the shade — gathering, choosing, reading
A Roman surveyor stretches a straight cord between stakes to lay out a new town grid, while a crowned figure watches from a dais — straight line and rule in one scene
A weaver's yard: one figure folds a long dyed cloth into neat layers, another braids three cords into a rope; a basket woven from interlaced reeds
A Roman army camp: soldiers stretch the ropes of a leather tent, an archer draws a bow taut nearby; lines of tension crossing the scene
A Roman magistrate walking with a line of attendants following in order, footprints showing the sequence; a smaller child copying the last step
A cloister courtyard closed on all sides by arches, a monk turning a large iron key in a gate; inside a garden, outside dusty road
A woodcutter's clearing: one tree cleanly felled with a clear axe cut, a carpenter trimming a plank with precise strokes; a pair of iron shears on a stump
An autumn orchard terrace at sunset: leaves and a few apples falling, two dice tumbling on a step, the sun setting over the western edge of the plinth
A road ends at a tall boundary stone tied with a blue finish ribbon.
A pool reflecting a willow whose branches bend to the water; a craftsman bends a heated wooden strip into a hoop over a fire, a bronze mirror catching light
Two oxen under one wooden yoke at a crossroads where two roads join; a carpenter's joint of two beams beside the field
A Roman memory-palace plan with a giant red map pin; an orator plants the pin on a circled spot.
An orator mid-speech, mouth open and arms out, a scribe with a scroll, and a theatre mask.
An officer hands a sealed scroll to a youth; the cape is vermillion.
A youth holds a Roman wax tablet on a mint mosaic floor while a mentor points toward a temple.
A family stands at a memorial bust, a lavender cloth and flowers beside it.
Geese raise the alarm beside a Juno Moneta coin and temple.
An hourglass between a withering plant and a new sprout.
A ewe with a newborn lamb, and a seed sprouting in the cut soil.
An infant on naming day, a gold bulla amulet on a cord.
A huge nova hangs over an entire cobalt night pavement that covers the plinth.
A merchant counts on a bronze abacus.
Armour being put on, everything made ready before action.
A scored loaf being broken into shared portions.
A patient endures on a wine-rose couch while a physician holds the wrist.
Rowers mid-stroke drive a ship through a cyan sea.

meaning: to seek, aim at, rush at
scene: Runners rush a magenta track toward the finish post.
A farmer overflows an amphora from an amber mound of grain.
A fisherman grasps a fish with both hands beside a copper heap of net.
A lantern-seeker stands on yellow light-washed ground.
A scholar points at a violet constellation board beside a globe.
A reaper sickle cleanly parts a sheaf in two on a chartreuse field.
A watchman in a bronze-ochre robe holds a torch on a parapet.
A signifer raises a huge crimson standard on crimson brick.
Two nearly identical statues stand on matching pedestals.
Hands untie a rope knot beside a wide turquoise bowl.
An orator shouts under an arch, sound-wave rings visible in the air.
Banquet guests take food from golden platters.
A fingertip touches a marble sphere on a coral contact disc.
A farmer stands on stepped terracotta earth terraces.
A figure twists a copper rope until it becomes a torch.
A farewell handshake beside a large emerald shield.
Winged Victory places a laurel crown on a kneeling victor; a palm leaf lies on the purple ground.
Green plants revive after watering, next to a wilted stub.
A huge papyrus scroll unrolls across the plinth.
A trust handshake on a sapphire altar, a loyal dog beside them.
A figure stands in a huge teal bowl marked like a clock face, a wooden rod set in the centre hole.
A figure in a well lifts a gold mirror; a checked gold coin rests on the rim.
A white-haired judge sits on a carved chair while two youths stand on a blue floor.
Several figures raise their right hands around a stone table on a green floor.
One figure sets a red cap on another head; a broken chain lies on the red ground.
A figure carries a huge purple sack while a purple fruit falls beside them.
A figure presses a gold lever and lifts a stone ball on the other end.
A shield-bearer stands on a yellow fortress wall; below, one figure rests a hand on a companion.
A sailor rows a small sailboat across a blue sea past a tiny island.
A figure kneels toward a huge yellow star, a small flag planted beside them.
Two people point at a bust on a table, recognizing who it is.
A kneeling figure offers a gift with a bow; the seated person rests a hand on the chest.
A figure stands on the sand before a high blue wave and a small boat.
A balance holds equal weights, with extra weights on the blue ground.
A plant shows its roots while a figure watches and a ball falls along a dotted path.
Two hills each hold a fire; a figure tends the nearer one with a stick.
A figure on a grey watchtower looks through a spyglass.
A figure leans into a green microscope; tiny shapes sit on the slide.
A crowd of small figures fills a red ground among several columns.
A green carriage is filled with people inside and on the roof.
A unicorn stands on a purple ground while two figures sit together.
A figure lights a birthday candle beside a calendar, inside a blue ring.
A teacher in a red robe stands and speaks while a student sits with a wax tablet.
One figure stands alone in front; a wreath rests on a small table, three others wait behind.
A huge red statue stands on a plinth while a tiny figure looks up.
A father rests a hand on a child; ancestor busts stand beside them.
A mother holds an infant, a city rising on the hill behind her.
A crowd stands in a ring, each holding a tablet, a flag in the middle.
A white dove carries an olive sprig over a blue floor and a stone table.
A green snake sheds its skin while a small figure watches.
A jointed purple figure walks by itself beside a real person.
Three figures stand from large to small on a red ground.
A row of shield-bearers stands in order.
Three workers hoist a stone ball with a teal crane.
One figure offers a pink gift; the other clasps their hands, pleased.
Three figures stand on a bridge; the one in teal is in the middle.
A figure runs toward a blue abacus, loaves lined up on the ground.
A cutaway shows tree roots and a radish while someone digs.
A figure kneels on purple ground before a temple altar.
Three fish leap from the water and a child jumps with them.
Two figures climb a flight of blue stairs.
One figure sits in a pink chair while others sit in front.
A figure sits alone on a rock in the sea, playing a pipe.
Two figures pull a rope tight between them.
A weaver works a loom that spills a purple cloth.
